High level options we recommend evaluating in parallel:

2) Private (VPC / customer-managed) for PHI-bound workloads that must not transit Redwood-managed network egress or must be behind customer KMS/HSM. This can be deployed into your VPC via an air-gapped/on-prem package if required.

Irene / Maria —

Quick sizing sketch based on the numbers Maria shared:
- Steady-state 12k/day -> ~0.14 RPS average, but we size to peaks.
- Peak 200 QPS for 15 minutes: assume 50% of requests hit the heavy model path (2k context).

Assumptions:
- Model: 13B/70B family tradeoff. We'll show two paths (13B opt, 70B quant).
- A100 80GB effective throughput: ~140 tokens/sec for 70B quantized (conservative), 400 tokens/sec for tuned 13B FP16/quant.
- Typical tokens per second requirement (avg request -> 1500 tokens total including generation): 1500 tokens / req -> at 200 QPS full concurrency that's 300k tokens/sec sustained during peak

Sizing options (peak-focused):
Option A — Dedicated (cost/predictable):
- For 70B quant: need ~3-4 A100 80GB equivalents for the burst window with intelligent batching and KV caching (we recommend 4 to keep latency SLAs).
- For 13B tuned: 1x A100 + 1x RTX8000-equivalent may be enough with continuous batching.
- Suggest reserved pool scaled to handle 2x expected peak for safety (burst ladder + overflow to lower-priority pool).

Option B — Private (VPC / on-prem variant for PHI):
- If PHI traffic is low (<=20%): operate PHI on a private VPC cluster sized for its peak (1-2 A100s depending on model) and non-PHI on Dedicated.
- If PHI traffic is high or residency demands on-prem: advise an on-prem cluster with identical node types; engineer will recommend 2x redundancy (active-passive) for updates and KV caching warm starts.

Operational notes:
- Recommend prefix/KV caching for user session continuity to reduce per-token ops for repeated queries. That can cut effective token throughput by ~30% for many workflows.
- Autoscaling: Dedicated supports fast burst via reserved burst capacity (we can guarantee warm nodes within 2-5 min with reserved commit). Private on-prem will have slower spin-up; plan for capacity headroom.

Cost back-of-envelope (monthly):
- Dedicated (4x A100 reserved): ~$XXk/month (detailed calc in attached capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx)
- Private on-prem (2x A100 + infra): CAPEX heavy + ops costs; recommend procurement alignment if customer wants this route.

I'll prepare a two-track proposal (Pilot: 1x dedicated A100 for non-PHI + 1x private A100 for PHI pilot, Scale: reserved dedicated pool + private VPC cluster if needed).

Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the split and timeline. Recommendation and next steps below (confidential):

Recommendation (pilot):
- Pilot split: deploy PHI into a private VPC deployment inside your cloud account (customer VPC connector) with 1x A100 80GB node reserved for PHI traffic. This ensures keys and egress controls remain under MediTrust control.
- Non-PHI pilot: one Dedicated A100 node in a reserved burst pool (managed by Redwood) with KV caching enabled and model pinned to a tuned 13B for low-latency interactions.
- Rationale: reduces procurement & CAPEX for pilot while meeting residency and compliance constraints. If PHI % increases during pilot, scale the private pool to 2x A100.

Longer-term (scale):
- If usage grows as expected and PHI remains >25%, recommended topology is hybrid: Private VPC cluster (2x A100 active + passive) for PHI + Dedicated reserved pool (4x A100 equiv) for general traffic with automated routing policies and fallback to lower-cost model variants during extreme peaks.
- SLA / procurement: Marissa will produce a joint quote covering both reserved Dedicated capacity and Private on-boarding/support fees. Vivek will own the SOC2/KMS integration checklist and will provide the SOC2 excerpt and KMS architecture diagram.
